ground_truth_recall_audit.milestone: Dropped support for Python 3.8 and raised the minimum dependency versions to the latest feature releases
Added a configuration option to control whether Flask automatically answers OPTIONS requests
Flask.open_resource, open_instance_resource and Blueprint.open_resource take an encoding parameter for text mode, defaulting to utf-8
Request.max_content_length can be customized per request instead of only through the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH config, and new MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE and MAX_FORM_PARTS configs were added
Added support for the Partitioned cookie attribute through the SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED config
Changed .env loading so that -e path takes precedence over the default .env and .flaskenv files
Added secret key rotation with the SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS config
Fixed how host_matching=True and subdomain_matching=False interact with SERVER_NAME
Request.trusted_hosts is now checked during routing and can be set through the TRUSTED_HOSTS config

narrative_precision_audit.narrative_claim: The journey begins with a series of updates to the GitHub Actions workflows
This commitment to keeping CI/CD tools up-to-date is crucial for ensuring compatibility with the latest features and security patches
A significant theme in the recent commits is the ongoing effort to manage and upgrade development dependencies
The commitment to dependency management continued with the merge commit which consolidated updates from the 3.0.x branch
The evolution of the codebase also reflects a commitment to improving code quality and type safety
Overall, the recent commits to the Flask repository illustrate a robust and proactive approach to software development
